How it works

From a Google listing to a shot list in four steps

1

Paste the basics

Drop in whatever you can grab — a Google Business listing, an About page, even just a name and city. Messy is fine.

2

Verify with AI research

We generate a research prompt that forces the AI to return sourced, checkable facts as JSON — never invented prices or dishes.

3

Pick a cinematic template

Sixteen story templates — slow burn, flame and char, doors open, one dish start to finish — each tuned to a pace and a video model.

4

Get your shot list

Shot-by-shot prompts, a reference photo checklist, and a downloadable pack — ready to hand to an AI video model or a real crew.

Built for real production

Every shot is grounded in your own reference photos

Upload photos of the dishes, the room, the plating style — the tool rotates them intelligently across shots so nothing repeats identically, and flags exactly when you need one more angle.

  • Camera, lens, and pacing language written into every prompt
  • Model-specific quirks and limitations handled automatically
  • Logos, menus, and prices flagged as post-production overlays, never generated
Any restaurant, any style

Steakhouse to street food, fine dining to food truck

Sixteen templates map to the pace and tone of your concept, and every model preset — Veo, Sora, Kling, Hailuo, Gemini and more — gets prompts written to fit exactly how that model behaves.

  • Autosaves as you go — refresh the page and pick up right where you left off
  • Export a ZIP with every prompt and every reference photo, ready to share
  • Nothing you type is ever sent anywhere — it all stays in this browser

The template sets the shot count and lengths. Everything after it — script beats, asset list, prompts — is derived from those slots.

Everything you enter is saved automatically in this browser, so a refresh or coming back later returns you to the same page with the same data. Nothing is sent anywhere.

Build the research prompt

Paste whatever you can grab from the restaurant's Google listing, website, or delivery page. The tool wraps it in a research prompt that forces the AI to return only sourced, checkable facts as JSON — never invented prices.

Paste raw restaurant details

Google Business listing, About page, menu page, delivery app copy, recent reviews. Messy is fine. Even just a name and city works.

Look it up first Google Maps — search the place, copy the address, hours and review count, then paste them above.

Your research prompt

Copy this into Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity with web search switched on. Ask for the JSON only.

Open and paste into Gemini Claude ChatGPT Perplexity

Bring the answer back

Paste the JSON the AI returned. Code fences and stray commentary are stripped automatically.

Quick open Gemini

Restaurant bio

Fill in what you have and leave the rest. More detail means a richer script, but nothing here is required. The one thing tracked separately is prices: an unconfirmed price stays out of on-screen text until you mark it verified.

Identity

Location and contact

Social profiles

Full links, starting with https. These get scanned in Step 2 for the brand's existing look.

Story

How it looks on camera

Step 2 turns these into lighting, lens and set-dressing choices, so keep them concrete.

Ratings and what reviewers say

Menu

Dish names alone are enough to build a shot list. Add a price plus the link it came from when you want that number to appear on screen — those are the ones marked verified.

Mark one dish ⭐ Hero product to build the whole reel around it — every food shot then features that one item instead of rotating through the menu.

Campaign brief

What this particular reel has to do. This decides the template more than the cuisine does — the same restaurant needs a different cut for an opening night than for a Tuesday delivery push.

The job

Generation engine

Clip limits differ by model, and they change often. Set the longest single clip your model reliably produces — slots longer than that get flagged so you can split them.

Presenter or on-camera model — optional

Off by default — every shot stays hands-only, faces soft or out of frame, same as the "Keep out" field above. Turn this on only when you have a real, rights-cleared photo of a person to feature: yourself, a staff member or owner, or one of the two licensed presets below.

Choose a photo. This exact photo is what every shot prompt below is told to match — same face, same expression, never a reinvented one.

Voice, music & sound effects — optional

Off by default, same as everywhere else here — nothing is assumed. Turn on only what you actually plan to add; leave the rest silent and add it in post.

Template

Ranked against the bio and the brief. The template fixes the shot count, the length of each beat and the job each shot does — the script gets written into these slots, not around them.

Style lock

Paste this block into every shot prompt, word for word, without editing it between shots. Shot-to-shot drift is what makes AI reels look stitched together — one fixed look block is the cheapest fix there is.

ComfyUI — generate template thumbnails

Point this at your local ComfyUI server (started with --enable-cors-header) to generate a thumbnail for any template. The prompt is pre-filled from the template style lock — once it renders, the image is pulled back automatically and applied as that template's thumbnail. No manual file copying.
